summary: lastIndexOf searches backward for the last strictly equal element and returns its zero-based index.
documentation: lastIndexOf searches backward for the last strictly equal element and returns its zero-based index. If there is no match the result is -1. Unlike findLast, it returns a position and takes a value rather than a predicate.
inputs: An object with events (array of strings) and target (string).
caution: Strict equality does not match NaN. Objects compare by identity, so this problem uses strings.
scenarios: Locate the latest retry marker in a local event list.
Find the last occurrence of a repeated navigation label.
Resume processing after the final matching checkpoint.
title: Locate the last checkpoint
problem: Input is {events, target}. Return the last index whose event equals target, or -1 when it never occurs.
goal: Use Array.lastIndexOf() or an equivalent approach demonstrating the same premise.
hint: Do not reverse the array: its original indices are the required output.
